words.sense: Make a person comply through threats, intimidation or fear of serious punishment.
misconceptions: Ignoring an explicit threat because it was delivered politely.

words.sense: Make action necessary or irresistible through a rule, circumstance or strong reason, without requiring intimidation.
misconceptions: Treating any necessary action as the product of threats.

semantic_axes.description: Coerce uses threats or intimidation to secure compliance; compel makes action necessary without necessarily threatening anyone.

edges.boundary_rule: Coerce uses threats or intimidation to secure compliance; compel makes action necessary without necessarily threatening anyone.

chains.frame: Which word best describes how Daria obtained Amir’s signature?

beats.text: Daria explained that joining the club required Amir to sign the consent form, so he reluctantly agreed.
beats.decisive_clue: a club requirement made signing necessary
beats.reason: A club requirement made signing necessary. Make action necessary or irresistible through a rule, circumstance or strong reason, without requiring intimidation..

beats.text: She also privately threatened to publish his messages if he refused to sign.
beats.decisive_clue: a private threat of exposure made refusal frightening
beats.reason: A private threat of exposure made refusal frightening. Make a person comply through threats, intimidation or fear of serious punishment..

chains.feedback_short: A private threat of exposure made refusal frightening makes coerce the better fit.
chains.feedback_deep: Coerce means make a person comply through threats, intimidation or fear of serious punishment; compel means make action necessary or irresistible through a rule, circumstance or strong reason, without requiring intimidation. Here, a private threat of exposure made refusal frightening; that is why coerce wins even after the new detail.
chains.contrast_rule: Coerce uses fear; compel can use necessity.
